lead.headline: Paul George Drops 36 in Philly as Celtics Take the East Lead
lead.subhead: Traded in the summer blockbuster, George walked into his old arena and hit six threes, including 14 points in the fourth, in a 123-101 Boston win. The Celtics are 9-2, best in the East. New jersey, same killer instinct.

articles.hed: Dame Time Returns as Portland Runs Past OKC
articles.body: Damian Lillard scored 13 of his 25 in the third quarter and sat the fourth as the Trail Blazers beat the Thunder 123-103, only their second win over OKC in 21 meetings. One hot quarter flipped a tied game into a rout.

articles.hed: Cousins Goes Home to Minnesota at the Deadline
articles.body: The Vikings brought Kirk Cousins back from Las Vegas for a 2027 third-round pick, one of six final-day deals as 18 in-season trades closed out the 2026 deadline. Sometimes the best move is the one you already know works.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Wednesday, the day of Mercury. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Mercury is the messenger: speed, wit, the right words at the right moment. Breathe slow so you can talk sharp.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go take Wednesday.

mindset.hed: Walk Into the Building and Score
mindset.body: Paul George got traded, walked back into the arena he used to call home, and dropped 36. Nobody handed him the moment; he took it in the fourth quarter. Midweek is where the grinders separate from the talkers. Every call today is a chance to take the fourth quarter. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Wednesday, the day of Mercury: run this right after Morning Charge. It's damp and about 41° outside, so keep the RipStick finisher indoors today. Quick hands, quick reps.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: Grok 4.8 finishes pretraining, soft rollout to Grok Bot this week
items.body: Musk confirmed Grok 4.8 is done pretraining and in reinforcement learning, with a gradual rollout to Grok Bot users later this week after xAI rewrote its training and inference stack.

items.hed: Apple building 'Harbor' to run AI models locally on Macs
items.body: A leaked Apple app turns a Mac into a private AI server for open-weight models, and can pool several Macs over Thunderbolt 5 to run bigger models. Nothing leaves your hardware.

items.hed: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow; OpenAI opens Businesses in ChatGPT
items.body: Anthropic plans to list on Nasdaq under ANT and also rolled out Claude Whiteboards, Sheets and Data. OpenAI put Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, letting companies claim listings and run agents.
Boston hit 22 threes and moved to 9-2, best in the East. Payton Pritchard added 18.

items.hed: Knicks roll Bucks 117-85; Towns double-double streak hits 14
items.body: Karl-Anthony Towns had 21 and 16, Jalen Brunson scored 23, and New York won for the sixth time in seven games.

items.hed: Suns hit season-high 22 threes; Franz Wagner drops 33
items.body: Phoenix routed the Clippers 133-110, Giannis had 30 and 11 in Miami's win at Utah, and Wagner's season high snapped Orlando's skid in Sacramento.
Final-day deals sent Kirk Cousins to Minnesota, Josh Downs to Kansas City, Keenan Allen to San Francisco and Amani Hooker to Buffalo.

items.hed: Colts keep Jonathan Taylor as deadline passes
items.body: Indianapolis moved Downs and Allen but held onto its star running back; the full rundown of all 18 deals and what they cost.

items.hed: Bears' early Simmons blockbuster still the deadline's biggest swing
items.body: Chicago landed Jeffery Simmons before the rush; PFT's tracker covers every deal and rumor from deadline week.

items.hed: Hokit plans to drown Gane in pace at UFC 334
items.body: The unbeaten challenger (10-0) says he'll push forward, wrestle and drag the champion into deep waters Saturday at MSG. Chris Weidman is picking Hokit.
Alatengheili replaces Adrian Yanez against Juan Diaz, and Sadykhov vs. Nascimento is off the card.

items.hed: UFC 334: all you need to know
items.body: Gane makes his first undisputed defense; Amanda Nunes returns against Kayla Harrison, and Stephen Thompson meets Charles Radtke on the prelims.

Wednesday belongs to Mercury, the Roman Hermes: messenger, trader and patron of quick minds and good deals. Old grimoires set it aside for workings of speech, commerce and learning. A sales day if there ever was one: say it clearly and ask for the close.

items.hed: Hermes Trismegistus and the Corpus Hermeticum
items.body: The Hermetic texts teach that mind (Nous) shapes the world, and that the one who knows himself knows the All. The practical edge: what you hold steady in your head shows up in how you carry the room.

A cobbler in 1600, Boehme saw sunlight glint off a pewter dish and said the whole hidden order of things opened to him. He kept making shoes and kept writing. Revelation doesn't require quitting the day job.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.hed: A soft answer, a sharp edge
grimoire.body: Solomon wrote: 'A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger' (Proverbs 15:1). In sales the calm voice wins the objection. Meet pushback with steadiness, not heat, and the deal stays alive.
grimoire.practice: Today, when someone pushes back, slow your voice down and ask one question before you answer.
